input.summary: New evidence changes the diagnosis: run 42558304970 at sha 08aa8c2c (my appended workflow-contract test) completed success, yet PR #226 head_sha is 6a4455b1 and branch tree shows venice-audit-bot's commit 60b4d6cc — so the job's own 'Commit regenerated matrices' step pushed again after every green run. The exact-head merge gate can therefore never be met while the job pushes: each run regenerates a diff (build output is not stable against the committed state) and moves the head to a sha that has no run. This turn removes the push from the job (keeping the guarded diff check as a non-pushing drift report) and tightens the test to forbid 'git push' in the workflow, so the next push produces a run at a head that stays put.
input.next: Next turn call branch_head('venice/repo-requirements-audit-v1') and runs('venice/repo-requirements-audit-v1') together; the head must equal the commit returned by this turn's workflow edit, and the newest run's sha must equal that head with conclusion success and no error annotation. If matched, call merge_pr(226, expected_head_sha=<that head>); if the head moved again, read run_jobs on the newest run to see whether the drift-report step or tests failed.

contribution.description: Root cause of the unmet exact-head merge gate proven from returned data: run 42558304970 is green at sha 08aa8c2c, but PR #226 head_sha is 6a4455b1 and the branch tree at 60b4d6cc is the bot's own 'audit: regenerate matrices' commit - the job pushes a regenerated diff on every run, so a green run's sha can never equal the head. Fix: make the diff check a non-pushing drift report and forbid git push in the workflow contract test.

pitfalls.problem: Every push run regenerates docs/venice-audit-v1 outputs into a state that differs from the committed files, so the guarded commit step pushes a new head (187168f5, 60b4d6cc, then 6a4455b1) after each green run; the green run's sha is never the branch head and the exact-head merge gate can never pass by polling.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Repeatedly forcing fresh runs from allowed paths while leaving the job's git push in place.
pitfalls.lesson: When a workflow job pushes its own build output, no push-triggered run can certify the head it creates. Remove the push from the job (report drift instead) or make the build byte-stable; verify the head stops moving before attempting merge_pr.

pitfalls.problem: build_gantt.py opened with a single-quoted multi-line string, so importing it from build_matrices.py raised SyntaxError and the Build matrices step exited 1 (run 42553625095).
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trusting the write_file ok=true receipt as proof the Python source parses.
pitfalls.lesson: A new module imported by build_matrices must start with a real docstring or comment; its first proof is the build step conclusion on the next push run, not the write receipt.
pitfalls.resolution: Docstring edit at 96ef7894 produced green run 42554257008.

pitfalls.problem: Unauthenticated job pages return 'This step has been truncated due to its large size' for every step, so the failing log line is never visible.
pitfalls.failed_approach: Trying to read the cause from the job HTML page.
pitfalls.lesson: Use run_jobs step conclusions plus the annotation list; never quote a log line that was not actually returned.
